## What's here

The data on this page come from the situation reports ("sitreps") that INSP,
the DRC's national public health institute, publishes on the outbreak. The
reports count cases by health zone, the district-sized unit the country's
health system is organised into, and health zones roll up into provinces.

Every number and every figure on this page is read from a file the pipeline
builds, at the moment the page renders. If a figure has no build rule behind
it, or a file hasn't been built yet, the render stops with an error, so nothing
here can be typed in by hand or left over from an old build. To rebuild it all
yourself, run `make build`, `make streams`, `make figures` and `make compare`.

```{python}
zt = load("data/build/series/zone_table.csv")
st = load("data/build/series/zone_table_status.csv")
cav = load("data/build/series/provisional_caveat.csv")
summ = load("data/build/series/province_summary.csv")
pro = load("data/build/series/prose_provinces.csv")
meta = load_json("data/build/streams/meta.json")

n_reports = st.height
# COUNTED BY WHAT THE REPORT PRODUCED, not by the exact status string. A
# report whose register entry rejects SOME of its columns still yields its
# zone rows -- sitrep 080 keeps a cumulative series that closes exactly --
# and testing `status == "ok"` would drop it from a sentence that claims to
# count every report printing a per-zone table.
n_zone = st.filter(pl.col("rows") > 0)["sitrep"].n_unique()
n_summ = summ["sitrep"].n_unique()
n_any = len(set(st["sitrep"]) & (set(zt["sitrep"]) | set(summ["sitrep"]) | set(pro["sitrep"])))
zrows = zt.filter(pl.col("level") == "zone").height
last = zt["date"].max()
itu = (zt.filter((pl.col("level") == "province")).sort("date")
       .filter(pl.col("cum_cases").is_not_null()))
Markdown(f"""
The archive holds **{stat(n_reports)} situation reports** (through {last}).
**{stat(n_zone)}** are read at health-zone level — every report that prints a
per-zone table — for **{stat(zrows)}** zone-day rows; the provincial summary
covers {stat(n_summ)} reports, and three early reports are read from their own
prose. Every held report contributes case data at the finest level its pages
print.
""")
```

```{python}
figure("data/build/figures/latest/availability.png")
```
![What each report states, at what geographic level (country, province or
health zone), and which table layout I read it
through.](../data/build/figures/latest/availability.png)

A few dates are worth keeping in your head as you read that figure. The
suspected-case and contact-tracing series stop at the start of June, which is
also when counts of confirmed deaths begin. On 13 July the reports start
splitting each day's deaths by how they were found: community deaths,
confirmed by a post-mortem swab, and deaths in treatment centres. And sitreps
084 to 086 use a layout that prints no per-zone table at all, so for those
three reports I only have province totals.

The reports annotate their own early numbers, and I treat those annotations as
data. Nearly every report from 004 through 033 carries a footnote saying its
headline cumulative count is still being harmonised, that is, reconciled
across the levels of the health system. From sitrep 026 (9 June) the footnote
also says which way the error runs. The count leaves out confirmed cases who
are still in the community and patients who escaped from care, so it is too
low. Sitreps 011 and 012 have a footnote saying the death count itself is
underestimated. Later, from sitrep 060 to 083, the reports warn that the last
few days' changes should be read with caution, because notifications arrive
late and the data are still being consolidated. Each of these statements is a row in `provisional_caveat.csv`,
whose `kind` column says which sort of caveat it is: `harmonisation_pending`
(still being harmonised), `harmonisation_undercount` (being harmonised, and
stated to be too low), `deaths_underestimated`, or `recent_data_provisional`
(the warning about recent days, flagged "caveat" in the index). The index below flags them
report by report. This matters if you fit the first four weeks of the
outbreak, because you'd be fitting numbers the source itself called
provisional, and from 9 June called too low.

## Index of situation reports

```{python}
ex = source("registers/reconciliation_exceptions.tsv")
rej = source("registers/rejected_routes.tsv")
cavd: dict[int, set] = {}
for s, k in cav.select("sitrep", "kind").iter_rows():
    cavd.setdefault(s, set()).add(k)
exset = set(ex["sitrep"].cast(pl.Int64))
rejset = set(rej["sitrep"].cast(pl.Int64))

rows = []
for r in st.sort("sitrep").iter_rows(named=True):
    n = r["sitrep"]
    marks = []
    kinds = cavd.get(n, set())
    if "recent_data_provisional" in kinds:
        marks.append("caveat")
    if "harmonisation_undercount" in kinds:
        marks.append("stated undercount")
    elif "harmonisation_pending" in kinds:
        marks.append("harmonisation")
    if "deaths_underestimated" in kinds:
        marks.append("deaths understated")
    if n in exset:
        marks.append("exception")
    if n in rejset:
        marks.append("route rejected")
    rows.append(
        f"| {n:03d} | {r['date']} | {r['table'] or '—'} | {r['rows']} "
        f"| {r['identity'] or '—'} | "
        f"{'' if r['residual'] in (None,) else r['residual']} "
        f"| {', '.join(marks)} |")
Markdown(
    "One row per report. *Route* is the table layout it was read through "
    "(`—` when no zone table exists); *identity* asks whether the page's own "
    "arithmetic closes; *flags* mark the source's own provisionality caveat, "
    "a hand-verified exception, or a rejected route.\n\n"
    "| report | date | route | rows | identity | residual | flags |\n"
    "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n" + "\n".join(rows) + "\n\n"
    ": Index of situation reports {#tbl-sitreps}")
```

## One primary source, and two readings I only check against

The primary source is the set of situation-report PDFs that INSP (Institut
National de Santé Publique) posts at `insp.cd`. I download them and pin each
one with a committed index and a manifest of SHA-256 hashes, so I can tell if
a file ever changes. Then I read the numbers from the table geometry drawn in
the PDF itself.

Two other groups have read the same documents. INRB-UMIE, the national
laboratory, keeps its own transcription, and epiforecasts has a scan. I use
both only as checks; nothing on this page is built from them. Since all three
of us read the same pages, agreement between us tells you the transcription is
right. It tells you nothing about whether the counts themselves are right. A
disagreement, on the other hand, always means something: either one of the
readings has an error, or two versions of a revised report were read.

```{python}
dis = load("data/build/compare/inrb_disagreements.csv")
scan = load("data/build/compare/scan_comparison.csv")
cm = load_json("data/build/compare/compare_meta.json")["inrb"]
figure("data/build/figures/latest/comparison.png")
Markdown(f"""
Against INRB-UMIE, per zone-day: **{stat(cm["cases_equal"])} of
{stat(cm["cases_compared"])}** case values agree exactly and
{stat(cm["deaths_equal"])} of {stat(cm["deaths_compared"])} death values;
**{stat(dis.height)}** rows disagree on either, each recorded with both
values. The denominator is the inner join of the two lineages —
**{stat(cm["ours_unmatched"])} of our {stat(cm["ours_zone_days"])} zone-day
rows have no INRB counterpart** and sit outside every agreement figure, and
they are not random: the INRB series currently ends {cm["inrb_last_date"]},
ours {cm["ours_last_date"]}, so the most recent reports are uncompared by
construction. Against the epiforecasts scan, the national cumulative agrees
on **{stat(scan.filter(pl.col('diff') == 0).height)} of {stat(scan.height)}**
reports exactly. The largest disagreement is not ours: sitrep 032 prints
Rwampara at 159 twice over — in its table and its narrative — where the INRB
file carries 192.
""")
```

## Every table is checked against the page's own arithmetic

Every table I extract has to add up the way the page says it does. A
province's health-zone rows, plus any rows the source counts but hasn't
assigned to a zone yet, must equal the province total printed on the page, and
the provinces must add up to the printed national total. When they don't, I
assume the mistake is mine until reading the page shows otherwise.

Sometimes the page really doesn't add up. When that happens the judgement goes
into a register, a hand-kept file with one row per judgement. Each row is tied
to the SHA-256 hash of that exact PDF, and it excuses that one gap on that one
document and nothing else.

```{python}
rec = load("data/build/series/province_series_reconciliation.csv")
t = dict(rec.group_by("reconciled").len().iter_rows())
Markdown(f"""
Province-reports: **{stat(t.get('ok', 0))} reconcile exactly**,
{stat(t.get('verified_exception', 0))} carry a hand-verified exception (the
page disagrees with itself, read and recorded), {stat(t.get('fails', 0))}
disagree and remain open, {stat(t.get('not_checkable', 0))} print no total to
check against.
""")
```

This check has a blind spot. It only catches errors that break the
arithmetic. If I read the neighbouring column of a table by mistake, say
suspected cases instead of confirmed, that column adds up just as well, and
the check passes. Mistakes like that get caught another way: by tests that pin
the values of specific named reports, and by comparing the assembled series
against the printed totals, further down.

The streams that downstream models fit are weekly incidence per province. To
build them I take the cumulative count, carry the last known value forward
over days with no report, difference it, and bin the differences into weeks
counted from day 0 (`{python} meta["day0"]`). Two checks have to pass. The
total a stream emits has to equal exactly how far the cumulative count moved,
and the assembled grid is compared against every province row the reports
print.

```{python}
lines = []
for name, r in sorted(meta["reconciliation"].items()):
    if r.get("kind") in ("care", "notified", "excluding_backlog"):
        # Reconciliation shapes this table's "emitted vs moved" framing does
        # not fit: care-ledger streams have their own figure (care_ledger.png)
        # and a different check (census/admissions/exits, not a cumulative
        # movement); notified and backlog-excluded streams check a distinct
        # identity (vs_cumulative, differenced_total) this table's columns do
        # not carry. Skipped rather than forced into columns that would
        # misrepresent what was checked -- not shown here, not silently
        # unchecked upstream.
        continue
    if r.get("kind") == "stock":
        # A reading at an instant: no accumulation window, so no emitted-vs-
        # moved identity to report — the span is the series' own extent.
        lines.append(
            f"| `{name}` | {r['n_obs']} | {stat(r['first_value'])} → "
            f"{stat(r['last_value'])} | — | stock, {r['first_date']} to "
            f"{r['last_date']} | — |")
        continue
    if "tests" in r:
        # The testing stream: licensed prose, checked against new cases.
        # Its daily companion carries province coverage instead.
        pv = r.get("positives_vs_new_cases")
        cov = r.get("n_provinces")
        lines.append(
            f"| `{name}` | {r['n_obs']} | {stat(r['positives'])} of "
            f"{stat(r['tests'])} tests | — | "
            + (f"{pv['n_equal']}/{pv['n_compared']} vs new cases | — |" if pv
               else f"{cov['min']}–{cov['max']} provinces/day | — |" if cov
               else "— | — |"))
        continue
    if "difference" not in r:
        # An ascertainment stream: community deaths of total split deaths,
        # read from the printed province rows and checked per-date against
        # the zone breakdown where the table prints one. The daily companion
        # carries no such check -- it IS the printed rows, per report day.
        av = r.get("vs_printed_daily")
        lines.append(
            f"| `{name}` | {r['n_obs']} | {stat(r['emitted'])} of "
            f"{stat(r['emitted_total'])} | — | "
            + (f"{av['n_equal']}/{av['n_compared']} daily | — |" if av else
               f"{r.get('n_flagged', 0)} flagged | — |"))
        continue
    vp = r.get("vs_printed", {})
    lines.append(
        f"| `{name}` | {r['n_obs']} | {stat(r['emitted'])} | "
        f"{r['difference']} | "
        f"{vp.get('n_equal','—')}/{vp.get('n_compared','—')} | "
        f"{vp.get('final_gap','—'):+d} |" if vp else
        f"| `{name}` | {r['n_obs']} | {stat(r['emitted'])} | "
        f"{r['difference']} | — | — |")
Markdown(
    "| stream | obs | emitted | vs source Δ | grid = printed | final gap |\n"
    "|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"
    ": Stream reconciliation. *vs source Δ* must be zero by construction; "
    "*grid = printed* counts report dates where the assembled cumulative "
    "equals the printed province row, and the *final gap* is the difference "
    "on the last report — zero for every stream. {#tbl-streams}")
```

## The registers hold the judgements I made by reading a page

Everything else in this repository is either downloaded or computed. The
registers are different. Each row is a judgement I made after reading a page.
Every row is keyed on the SHA-256 hash of the document it's about, so if INSP
revises a report, the hash stops matching and the row has to be judged again.
And each row excuses exactly one value, so if the value we read changes, the
excuse no longer covers it.

```{python}
zpo = source("registers/zone_province_overrides.tsv")
sno = source("registers/sitrep_number_overrides.tsv")
zal = source("registers/zone_aliases_local.csv")
ext = source("registers/external_sitreps.tsv")
Markdown(f"""
| register | rows | each row asserts |
|---|---|---|
| `reconciliation_exceptions.tsv` | {ex.height} | this page's printed rows do not sum to its printed total, by exactly this much |
| `rejected_routes.tsv` | {rej.height} | this route, on this document, reads the wrong table -- or reads the right one with named columns displaced |
| `zone_province_overrides.tsv` | {zpo.height} | the page states in words which province this row belongs to |
| `zone_aliases_local.csv` | {zal.height} | this printed spelling is that canonical health zone |
| `sitrep_number_overrides.tsv` | {sno.height} | this upload's filename misstates its report number or data date |
| `external_sitreps.tsv` | {ext.height} | INSP does not serve this report; it is held from a secondary archive and its PDF is committed, because nothing can fetch it again |
""")
```

## The care ledger

The reports also keep a ledger of the treatment centres, written out in words
for each province in the section on patient care. It gives admissions; exits,
and the four ways a patient can leave a centre; the census at the end of each
day, split into confirmed and suspected patients; and the number of beds
installed. `extract_care_prose.py` reads all of it into
`data/build/series/care_prose.csv`, and the release publishes it as the
`care_*` stream files, which the streams README lists. The confirmed census is
worth a look if you're fitting: it measures a state (how many confirmed
patients are in care at one moment), while the case and death streams measure
flows.

```{python}
figure("data/build/figures/latest/care_ledger.png")
```
![The care ledger, as the reports write it out in words. Panel A is why I
trust it. The front-page tile and the care section's sentence about the whole
response are two readings of the same page, made by two different extractors
in this repository, and wherever both print a census of confirmed patients in
isolation, they agree exactly. Panel B is occupancy against capacity for each
province. It's a ratio of sums, so it can't see one full centre inside a
half-full province. Panel C is the ledger itself, split into panels by the
passage that printed each value, and never summed across panels. Panel D is
every count of absconders (patients who left a centre without being
discharged) that the reports print, drawn as separate marks because that's
what the data are.](../data/build/figures/latest/care_ledger.png)

## What isn't here

I don't extract the laboratory, alerts or contact-tracing tables yet. The
reference pipeline reads them, and this one will. The care ledger comes from
the report text only. The reports also print a patient-movement table with the
same quantities per province, absconders included, and reading it would
roughly triple the absconder coverage you see in panel D. I also don't read
the daily suspected inflow from the front-page dashboard after 12 July, so the national suspected series ends where the early layout stops
printing it. The `{python} stat(dis.height)` disagreements with INRB are waiting to be
settled: I'll read each page, then decide case by case whether to report it
upstream. Finally, no fit uses these streams yet. That work belongs to the
modelling repository.
